claims.text: The driver never entered the pickup geofence. His own trace places him 559.37 m from the pin at his closest approach (driver_track.min_distance_m), more than eleven times the 50 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for a STANDARD zone, and derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 — not one of his 37 fixes falls inside the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the fee is not chargeable.

Independently of the geofence, the driver's dwell was zero. derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second minimum that POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires for a STANDARD pickup, so the waiting clock never started and no dwell had elapsed when the driver cancelled at 07:31:00. Limb (c) fails on its own and the conjunctive four-limb test in POL-NS-01 collapses.

POL-NS-06 states the arithmetic directly: an effective in-geofence dwell of 0 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum is a 300 second shortfall, and on that shortfall the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The driver cannot rescue the computation under POL-NS-06(i), because there are no separate in-geofence intervals to accumulate and no traffic advisory on file.

The 07:25:20 'arrived' marker is a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. At that timestamp the trace places the driver 559.37 m from the pin — far beyond the 300 m threshold — and his distinct speed is 0.0 km/h at a fixed standoff, so he was stationary, but not at the pickup. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies squarely: the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list.

POL-NS-03 cannot be used to soften this into a wrong-entrance case. That clause reaches only a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; the driver's closest fix was 559.37 m out, past the 400 m ceiling, so the clause does not engage at all. No venue-identity comparison is needed and no pin-ambiguity goodwill payment arises.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road and waiting window. EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, so its absence is itself citable: there is no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT on file, and nothing in the record explains the driver's 559 m standoff from the pickup point as a lawful reason to hold off the kerb.

The chat log does not place the car at the block. Its only driver message, at 07:25:40, is 'I have marked arrival.' — an assertion about the app marker, not about the vehicle's position — and the system's 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 07:25:21 merely repeats the same marker. Nothing in the record contradicts the rider's account that the car never came to the block, and the trace shows why: the driver was 559 m away the whole time.

No driver compensation is payable on these facts. POL-NS-07 funds compensation only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, while POL-NS-05(ii) says in terms that no compensation is payable where there is no qualifying in-geofence fix. On the profile side, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, well below the threshold POL-NS-07 names, so the anti-farming question does not arise.

This case does not rest on impaired evidence, so confidence in a full refund is not capped. The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, covers 100% of the window with 37 fixes at a 10 second cadence, carries no gaps (max gap 0 seconds), and the 07:25:20 arrival marker coincides exactly with a GPS fix timestamp, so there is no clock skew to discount the arrival finding under POL-GEN-02.

The money is fixed by the ledger: fare_breakdown shows a SGD 4.00 cancellation fee actually charged, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, against a SGD 0.00 base fare on a trip that never started. A full refund of that cancellation-fee line is the remedy, and it leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

claims.text: The rider's exonerating route under POL-NS-04 fails at limb (a). The chat log carries exactly two messages and neither was sent by the rider: MSG-09104-001 is the SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 07:25:21 and MSG-09104-002 is the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40. There is no rider message giving her own position, naming an entrance, block, tower or bay, asking where the driver is, or saying she cannot see the vehicle - so the coordinating message limb (a) requires simply does not exist in this window.

POL-NS-04 limb (c) also fails, and on the rider's own device. The rider track runs from 07:25:30 to 07:30:50 and places her 519.46 m from the pickup pin, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0 against a rider presence radius of 100 m for the STANDARD zone class. The rider was not waiting at the pickup point either, so her account that the car 'never came to my block' is not corroborated by her own trace.

The driver's record carries no anti-farming pattern on the two fields POL-NS-07 names and no others: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, short of the '4 or more' limb, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 120 is 0.008, short of the 0.08 limb. Because POL-NS-07 requires both limbs, its anti-farming branch does not trip on this driver, compensation is not withheld on that ground, and the escalation packet that branch prescribes - the one that directs the reviewer to refund the rider in full - is not engaged.

No abuse-based escalation trigger is available on the counters the policy actually reads. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so neither limb (c) nor limb (d) of POL-NS-09 fires, and the lifetime counters (prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot be substituted for them. This case falls to be decided on this trip's own evidence, not on either party's history.

The arrival event on this trip is not a bare, uncorroborated tap. The trip record records arrived_at 07:25:20 and a wait_time_min of 5.7 running to the 07:31:00 cancellation; the platform's own SYSTEM notification 'Your driver has arrived' went out at 07:25:21; the driver posted 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40; and his statement on file is that he 'marked arrival and waited before cancelling'. The trace, for its part, places the driver 559.37 m from the pin across the same interval. The driver did not leave and return - there are no gaps, max_gap_sec is 0.0 and trace_distance_km is 0.0 - so this is not a driver who took another job and came back. If the Judge finds these admissible artifacts in direct conflict over arrival and dwell, POL-NS-09(b) applies: the open question of which measure governs is for a human reviewer, and the SGD 4.00 fee is held rather than refunded while that review is pending.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the charge cannot stand. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold. Limb (b) requires the GPS trace to place the driver inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup at or before the 'arrived' event. It does not: the driver's own trace carries 37 fixes, all stationary (speeds 0.0 km/h), at a mean, minimum and maximum distance of 559.37 m from the pin, with derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count of 0. Limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of 300 seconds for a STANDARD zone; derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec is 0.0 seconds, so the waiting clock never started. The conjunctive test collapses and the fee is not chargeable. POL-NS-02 then gives the rider a full refund, and POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) cannot engage because the driver's closest approach, 559.37 m, is beyond that clause's 400 m ceiling — so no venue comparison and no pin-ambiguity goodwill payment arises.

POL-NS-05 applies on its own terms. At the 07:25:20 'arrived' marker the trace places the driver 559.37 m from the pin, far past the 300 m threshold, so the arrival marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. No qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, so POL-NS-05(ii) governs squarely: full refund of the cancellation fee, no compensation, and the trip recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver. That is the referral above. (POL-NS-06 would reach the same refund as a 300-second dwell shortfall; the arithmetic is not in dispute.)

On the driver's escalation argument. You contend the arrival tap, the platform's 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 07:25:21 and your 'I have marked arrival.' message at 07:25:40 conflict with the trace, so POL-NS-09(b) should send this to a human reviewer. POL-NS-09(b) requires that no clause resolves the conflict. POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves it: a marker set while the driver is more than 300 m from the pin is a false marker. The system notice and your own message do not supply an independent position fix — they restate the marker the trace contradicts — so they neither create an unresolved contradiction nor support arrival. The specific, datable position evidence wins.

On the rider's side. POL-NS-04 does not assist you: the chat log contains no rider message at all (only the system notice and the driver's message), and your own rider track shows no qualifying fix within the 100 m rider-presence radius. You do not need it — the refund follows from the driver's trace alone, and POL-NS-05(ii)/POL-NS-06 refund the fee whether or not the rider was present or responsive.

Compensation. None is payable. POL-NS-07 funds a driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full; it is not, and POL-NS-05(ii) states in terms that no compensation is payable where there is no qualifying in-geofence fix. The anti-farming question does not arise either way (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 120 completed trips in 30 days, below both limbs), and no abuse-based escalation fires (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0). The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09104-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) cannot help: POL-NS-06(i) needs a present, populated advisory to permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and there are no such intervals here.

Confidence. The deciding facts — driver position and absence of any qualifying in-geofence fix — are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record, both COMPLETE at weight 1.0, with 100% coverage, a 10-second cadence and no gaps, and the arrival marker coincides with a fix timestamp, so no impairment discount applies.
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record: record trip TRP-09104 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-09104.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged to the rider is refunded in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the fee cannot stand. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four POL-NS-01 conditions hold. They do not. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09104, weight 1.0, COMPLETE, 100% coverage, 37 fixes at a 10-second cadence, max gap 0 s) puts the driver at a fixed 559.37 m from the pickup pin for the whole interval, and derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 - not one of his 37 fixes falls inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. Limb (b) (inside the geofence at the arrival event) therefore fails, and independently limb (c) fails: the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 s against the 300 s STANDARD minimum, so the waiting clock never started. The conjunctive test collapses.

The arrival marker is false. The trip record's 'arrived' event at 07:25:20 carries a timestamp at which the trace places the driver well beyond the 300 m threshold. POL-NS-05 is exactly the clause that resolves an arrival marker against a GPS position, so the marker is FALSE. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies squarely: the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is referred as a false-arrival event against the driver. POL-NS-02 points the same way (no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation), and POL-NS-03 does not engage, because it reaches only a driver stationary within 400 m of the pin - the closest fix here was 559.37 m - so no pin-ambiguity goodwill and no wrong-entrance allocation arises.

On the driver's points. I accept that POL-NS-04 limb (a) fails (the chat log's only two messages are the SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' notice and the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' - there is no rider coordinating message), and that the rider's own track runs about 519 m from the pin with rider_qualifying_fix_count 0. Those facts do not change the outcome: POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-06 make the refund payable whether or not the rider was present or responsive, so her distance is immaterial to the fee. I accept that no POL-NS-07 or POL-NS-09 counter on the fields the policy actually reads fires (no_show_terminations_30d 1 and 1/120 = 0.008, both below the anti-farming limbs; rider no_show_disputes_30d 0; both counterparty counters 0). The lifetime counters (prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no weight.

I reject the driver's POL-NS-09(b) escalation argument. That trigger fires only where two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence and no clause resolves the conflict. POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves precisely this conflict - an arrival tap against a GPS position - so the trigger does not fire. For the same reason there is no impairment under POL-NS-08: the 07:25:20 marker coincides with a GPS fix (no clock skew), there are no trace gaps and 37 fixes, the chat log holds the 2 messages the trip record counts, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line matches the POL-NS-01 resolution rule (greater of the STANDARD zone fee 4.00 and the RYDE_X tier fee 4.00).

On the rider's points. I accept the geofence claim (POL-NS-02), the zero-dwell claim (POL-NS-01(c)), the false-arrival claim (POL-NS-05, which produces both the refund and the referral), the finding that POL-NS-03 does not engage, the point that the chat contains no statement placing the car at the block, the point that no POL-NS-07 compensation is funded, and the ledger point that the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line is the sum to return (base fare, platform fee and all other lines being 0.00).

Confidence. The deciding facts are carried by EV-GPS-09104 and EV-TRIP-09104, both at weight 1.0; no deciding artifact is below 1.0, so no discount applies and no escalation floor is approached. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09104-01, weight 0.0) carries no deciding fact and does not bear on the outcome.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is payable to the driver. The reason is arithmetic rather than a question of who to believe. POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four of its conditions hold, and two of them fail on the platform's own trace. Limb (b) requires the GPS to put the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before the arrival event: his nearest fix is 559.37 m from the pin (EV-GPS-09104, derived.driver_track.min_distance_m) and derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 across all 37 fixes, so not one reading falls inside the radius. Limb (c) requires a continuous 300 second in-geofence dwell: the longest qualifying run is 0.0 seconds. The conjunctive test therefore collapses and the fee is not chargeable. Because the 'arrived' marker was set while the driver was more than 300 m out, POL-NS-05 treats it as a false arrival marker; the waiting clock is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, there is none anywhere in the trip, and POL-NS-05(ii) directs the full refund, no compensation, and a false-arrival record against the driver — that last instruction is the referral above. The rider's claims on POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01, POL-NS-05 and on the money in EV-FARE-09104 are accepted, and her point that POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee is right: that clause only reaches a driver stationary within 400 m of the pin, and 559.37 m is past its ceiling, so no wrong-entrance or pin-ambiguity payment arises. Turning to the driver's claims: it is true that the rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 fails — the chat log holds only the system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and your own 'I have marked arrival.', so there is no coordinating message from the rider (limb (a)), and her own trace places her 519.46 m from the pin with 0 qualifying fixes (limb (c)). But POL-NS-04 is not the route to this refund, so defeating it changes nothing: the refund follows from the driver's own failed arrival under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05 and applies whether or not the rider was present or responsive. Your claim that the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip is accepted (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, well under 4, and the ratio is 0.008), as is your claim that POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire on the trailing-window counters. Your escalation argument under POL-NS-09(b) is not accepted. The trip record's arrived_at is a marker the driver set, not a second measurement of his position, and its tension with the trace is exactly the situation POL-NS-05 was written to resolve: limb (b) requires that 'no clause resolves the conflict', and POL-NS-05 resolves it. On evidence quality (POL-GEN-02): the deciding trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, covers 100% of the window with 37 fixes at a 10 second cadence and no gaps, and the 07:25:20 marker coincides with a GPS fix, so there is no clock-skew discount and confidence is not capped; the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09104-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but it carries nothing here — it could only have helped the driver's side by allowing separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and there are no such intervals. No escalation trigger is met: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the evidence does not conflict in a way no clause resolves, and no abuse counter is engaged. Lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags and prior_disputes_filed are context only under POL-GEN-01 and played no part.
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record TRP-09104 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-09104 — the 07:25:20 'arrived' marker was set with the driver's GPS 559.37 m from the pickup pin, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.

His own trace places him 559.37 m from the pin at his closest approach (driver_track.min_distance_m), more than eleven times the 50 m arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets for a STANDARD zone, and derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0 — not one of his 37 fixes falls inside the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the fee is not chargeable.

Independently of the geofence, the driver's dwell was zero. derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec is 0.0 seconds against the 300 second minimum that POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires for a STANDARD pickup, so the waiting clock never started and no dwell had elapsed when the driver cancelled at 07:31:00. Limb (c) fails on its own and the conjunctive four-limb test in POL-NS-01 collapses.

ledger.claim: The 07:25:20 'arrived' marker is a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. At that timestamp the trace places the driver 559.37 m from the pin — far beyond the 300 m threshold — and his distinct speed is 0.0 km/h at a fixed standoff, so he was stationary, but not at the pickup. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies squarely: the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list.

POL-NS-03 cannot be used to soften this into a wrong-entrance case. That clause reaches only a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; the driver's closest fix was 559.37 m out, past the 400 m ceiling, so the clause does not engage at all. No venue-identity comparison is needed and no pin-ambiguity goodwill payment arises.

ledger.claim: The chat log does not place the car at the block. Its only driver message, at 07:25:40, is 'I have marked arrival.' — an assertion about the app marker, not about the vehicle's position — and the system's 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 07:25:21 merely repeats the same marker. Nothing in the record contradicts the rider's account that the car never came to the block, and the trace shows why: the driver was 559 m away the whole time.

No driver compensation is payable on these facts. POL-NS-07 funds compensation only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, while POL-NS-05(ii) says in terms that no compensation is payable where there is no qualifying in-geofence fix. On the profile side, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, well below the threshold POL-NS-07 names, so the anti-farming question does not arise.

This case does not rest on impaired evidence, so confidence in a full refund is not capped. The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, covers 100% of the window with 37 fixes at a 10 second cadence, carries no gaps (max gap 0 seconds), and the 07:25:20 arrival marker coincides exactly with a GPS fix timestamp, so there is no clock skew to discount the arrival finding under POL-GEN-02.

The money is fixed by the ledger: fare_breakdown shows a SGD 4.00 cancellation fee actually charged, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, against a SGD 0.00 base fare on a trip that never started. A full refund of that cancellation-fee line is the remedy, and it leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

The rider's exonerating route under POL-NS-04 fails at limb (a). The chat log carries exactly two messages and neither was sent by the rider: MSG-09104-001 is the SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 07:25:21 and MSG-09104-002 is the driver's own 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40. There is no rider message giving her own position, naming an entrance, block, tower or bay, asking where the driver is, or saying she cannot see the vehicle - so the coordinating message limb (a) requires simply does not exist in this window.

POL-NS-04 limb (c) also fails, and on the rider's own device. The rider track runs from 07:25:30 to 07:30:50 and places her 519.46 m from the pickup pin, with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0 against a rider presence radius of 100 m for the STANDARD zone class. The rider was not waiting at the pickup point either, so her account that the car 'never came to my block' is not corroborated by her own trace.

The driver's record carries no anti-farming pattern on the two fields POL-NS-07 names and no others: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, short of the '4 or more' limb, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 120 is 0.008, short of the 0.08 limb. Because POL-NS-07 requires both limbs, its anti-farming branch does not trip on this driver, compensation is not withheld on that ground, and the escalation packet that branch prescribes - the one that directs the reviewer to refund the rider in full - is not engaged.

No abuse-based escalation trigger is available on the counters the policy actually reads. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so neither limb (c) nor limb (d) of POL-NS-09 fires, and the lifetime counters (prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot be substituted for them. This case falls to be decided on this trip's own evidence, not on either party's history.

The arrival event on this trip is not a bare, uncorroborated tap. The trip record records arrived_at 07:25:20 and a wait_time_min of 5.7 running to the 07:31:00 cancellation; the platform's own SYSTEM notification 'Your driver has arrived' went out at 07:25:21; the driver posted 'I have marked arrival.' at 07:25:40; and his statement on file is that he 'marked arrival and waited before cancelling'. The trace, for its part, places the driver 559.37 m from the pin across the same interval. The driver did not leave and return - there are no gaps, max_gap_sec is 0.0 and trace_distance_km is 0.0 - so this is not a driver who took another job and came back. If the Judge finds these admissible artifacts in direct conflict over arrival and dwell, POL-NS-09(b) applies: the open question of which measure governs is for a human reviewer, and the SGD 4.00 fee is held rather than refunded while that review is pending.
